title: manager-hiring-and-onboarding-playbook-2026
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Purpose

This playbook is a single-source-of-truth for Redwood managers running hiring loops, new-hire onboarding, and the first-year performance & feedback cycle. It consolidates operational SLAs, templates, interviewer expectations, and manager checklists so hires are predictable, inclusive, and successful.

Scope

- Audience: people managers at Redwood (IC leads, engineering managers, product managers, hiring managers).
- Applies to: full-time employees, contractors >6 months, and senior IC levels that require a manager-led loop.
- Not covered: campus hiring / intern programs (see intern-onboarding page) and executive hires (VP+/C-level).

High-level hiring SLA and timeline

1) Requisition approval: manager submits req in Workday — target approval within 3 business days.
2) Recruiter screen: recruiter contact within 3 business days of req approval.
3) Interview loop scheduled: target 10 business days from first recruiter-screen. If candidate is passive or exceptional, accelerate to 72 hours.
4) Decision window: hiring team provides feedback and recommendation within 48 hours of final interview.
5) Offer approval: manager obtains Budget + People Ops sign-off within 48 hours.
6) Offer extension: recruiter extends verbal offer same day approval is obtained; written offer within 24 hours.

Checklist: Before you open a requisition

- Confirm role scope, level, and hiring manager rationale with your manager.
- Confirm budget and headcount bucket with finance (cc: finance-ops@redwood.ai).
- Draft compelling job brief: responsibilities (5–7 bullets), success metrics (OKRs/90-day goals), must-have skills vs nice-to-have.
- Identify interview panel (diverse mix, at least one trained interviewer and one cross-functional stakeholder).
- Choose recruiting channels: internal referral, Greenhouse posting, and targeted outreach as needed.

Interview loop design (recommended, flexible)

- Stage 0: Recruiter screen (30 min) — role fit, salary band, logistics.
- Stage 1: Technical / skills deep-dive (60 min) — live coding or system design for eng; case study for product; portfolio review for design.
- Stage 2: Manager + behavioral (45–60 min) — ownership, collaboration, conflict, career aspirations.
- Stage 3: Cross-functional (45 min) — partner stakeholders for collaboration fit.
- Stage 4: Hiring committee / final calibration (30 min) — optional for senior roles.

Interviewer expectations and rubric

- All interviewers: complete Interviewer Training (L&D) and bias mitigation quick module.
- Use the standard rubric: Competency (0–3), Problem Solving (0–3), Communication (0–3), Role Fit (0–3).
- Passing score: median >= 2 across core competencies and no 0s in Problem Solving. For senior levels, require a strong endorsement from at least two interviewers.
- Provide written feedback in Greenhouse within 24 hours. Evidence-based comments required (what the candidate did/specified behavior).

Inclusive hiring best practices

- Two-question rule: at least two members must independently assess on each critical competency.
- Avoid creating culture-fit gates; use collaboration-fit examples (how they worked across teams).
- Use structured interviews (same stem questions for all candidates for a role).
- Provide accommodations on request and proactively ask if candidates need them.

Offer and negotiation guidance

- Compensation bands are defined per level in the compensation matrix (People Ops maintains). Always include total compensation breakdown (base, equity, bonus, sign-on).
- If extending above-band offers, pre-approve with People Ops and Finance.
- Standard approval SLA: manager -> director -> people-ops -> finance. Use the offer-approval template in Workday.
- Counter-offer guidance: prioritize candidate experience and speed; consult People Ops before countering material requests.

New hire 90-day onboarding plan (manager responsibilities)

Day 0 (before start)
- Confirm IT access requests: SSO, GitHub, Slack, Google Drive, internal tools.
- Send welcome message and first-day agenda.
- Assign buddy and schedule first-week socials.

Week 1 (orientation & context)
- Day 1: team intro, role-level expectations, basic repo walkthrough, set up dev environment.
- End of week 1: 30-minute 1:1 to check ramp blockers.

Weeks 2–4 (foundation & contribution)
- Assign a low-risk onboarding project with clear acceptance criteria.
- Weekly 1:1s focused on clarity of goals and early blockers.
- Technical/role training sessions scheduled as needed.

Days 30, 60, 90 (formal checkpoints)
- Day 30: manager sends written progress note (summary of work, blockers, alignment).
- Day 60: calibration meeting with manager’s manager and People Ops if concerns about ramp.
- Day 90: performance checkpoint (format below). Outcome: confirmed, extended probation, or role adjustment.

90-day performance checkpoint template

- Rating (Confirm / Needs Support / Role Adjustment)
- Evidence: list of deliverables and observable behaviors
- Development plan: specific goals for next 90 days and resources needed
- Stakeholders: buddy, cross-functional partners, direct manager

Manager playbook for continuous performance & feedback

Cadence and artifacts
- Weekly 1:1s (30–60 min) documented in Lattice. Managers must log agenda and outcomes.
- Quarterly performance reviews aligned with company OKR cadence.
- Mid-cycle calibration: managers submit calibration notes 1 week before calibration meetings.
- Career conversations: at least twice per year for every direct report.

Behavioral norms for managers

- Feedback: timely, specific, and balanced (situation, behavior, impact).
- Growth-focused: connect performance feedback to explicit skill-building actions and resources.
- Documentation: keep factual records of repeated behaviors and key decisions (do not store PII in Lattice comments).
- Escalation: if performance concerns persist after a documented 30–60 day plan, engage People Ops and legal as per the progressive-discipline policy.

Performance improvement plan (PIP) process overview

- Trigger: sustained underperformance despite coaching (documented over 30–60 days).
- Steps: manager drafts plan (specific goals + metrics) -> People Ops review -> 30–90 day PIP -> weekly check-ins -> final assessment.
- Rights and support: employee may request a representative (mentor/People Ops advocate). Senior leadership must approve terminations.

Manager templates and snippets

- Offer extension email (concise template)
- Interview cancellation/reschedule message
- First-week agenda (copy/paste)
- 30/60/90 checkpoint email template

Sample first-week agenda (copyable)

Mon: Welcome, paperwork, team intro, dev env setup
Tue: Product walkthrough, codebase orientation, buddy pairing
Wed: Small onboarding ticket, shadowing sessions
Thu: Cross-team introductions, Q&A with manager
Fri: Wrap-up, 1:1, set 30-day goals

Records, systems, and ownership

- Primary systems: Greenhouse (recruiting), Workday (offers/reqs), Lattice (performance), Slack (communication), Okta (SSO).
- Hiring owner: hiring manager (accountable). Recruiter: operational owner. People Ops: policy & approval owner.
- Document retention: interview notes retained per policy for 2 years unless candidate requests removal.

Common edge cases and guidance

- Internal transfers: manager starts an internal transfer form in Workday and consults with current manager before scheduling interviews.
- Multiple offers: prioritize candidate transparency. People Ops should mediate if cross-team conflicts arise.
- Re-hire within 12 months: treat as internal re-hire; consult finance for compensation parity.

Manager responsibilities checklist (one-line items)

- Define 90-day success criteria before first day.
- Confirm interview panel diversity and training.
- Share feedback within 48 hours post-interview.
- Ensure onboarding project is scoped and documented.
- Hold weekly 1:1 and log in Lattice.
- Run formal 30/60/90 checkpoints and document.
- Flag high-risk hires to People Ops by day 15.
